newsitem.title: UK: Proton takes control of Lotus.
newsitem.headline: Proton takes control of Lotus.

text.p: The Malaysian automaker Proton said Wednesday it agreed to pay about $83 million for an 80 percent stake in Lotus Group, the troubled British sports car maker once owned by General Motors Corp.
The deal ends months of uncertainty for Lotus, whose owner, Italian entrepreneur Romano Artioli, has been seeking a major investor for most of this year.
"Lotus is a legend -- it's a name that conjures excitement all over the world," said Yahaya Ahmad, chairman of Proton's parent DRB-HICOM and one of Malaysia's most influential businessmen.

Proton will pay 51 million British pounds ($83 million) for the stake and lend Lotus 13 million pounds ($21 million) to cover working capital. Under the agreement, Yahaya will take a 16.25 percent personal stake in Lotus Group alongside Proton's 63.75 percent interest, Proton said.

Started by auto racing engineer Colin Chapman in the early 1950s, Lotus was once a leading name in Grand Prix circuits, with drivers including Graham Hill, Jim Clark, Jochen Rindt, Emerson Fittipaldi and Mario Andretti winning world championships in Lotus cars.
Its vehicles included the Lotus Seven, the Elan, the Elite and its new model, the Elise.

Lotus was taken over by General Motors in 1986, and then piled up losses of 50 million pounds ($75 million) in the five years before its sale in 1993 to the parent of the Italian automaker Bugatti Automobili, which went into receivership, a form on bankruptcy, last year.
Proton said the change in ownership will not affect the way Lotus is managed, including its business of providing engineering and technology services to automotive and industrial clients.
Yahaya said Proton planned to boost production of Lotus' Elise sports car in England and would add production capacity in Malaysia.
"With our contribution we can expand Lotus production here ... we will expand capacity immediately," he told a news conference at Lotus' factory in eastern England.

Outgoing chairman Artioli told reporters, "I think I have done my part to ensure that Lotus can now expand its activities." Artioli owned Lotus through Luxembourg-registered Bugatti International SA, the parent of Bugatti Automobili.
